map.输入一组地质数据（逗号或空格分隔），计算均值、标准差、变异系数、置信区间等统计指: Enter a set of geological data (comma or space separated) and compute the mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, confidence interval and other statistics
map.样本概览：录入数据算均值、标准差、变异系数与置信区间: Sample overview: enter data to compute mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation and confidence interval
map.均匀性判断：用变异系数 CV 判定数据均匀/较均匀/不均匀: Uniformity assessment: use the coefficient of variation CV to classify data as uniform / fairly uniform / non-uniform
map.推断估计：按 t 分布给出总体均值的置信区间: Inferential estimate: give a confidence interval for the population mean from the t distribution
map.：算法：n、总和、均值 x̄；方差按总体(N)或样本(n−1)切换，标准差 σ=: : Algorithm: n, sum, mean x̄; variance switches between population (N) and sample (n−1), standard deviation σ=√variance; coefficient of variation CV=σ/x̄×100%; minimum, maximum, range, median, interquartile range IQR; standard error SE=σ/√n; confidence interval = x̄ ± t(α/2,n−1)·SE (t from the t distribution table by confidence level and degrees of freedom). Dispersion: CV<15% uniform, 15~30% fairly uniform, ≥30% non-uniform.
map.：例：10 个岩石密度测点 12.5,13.2,11.8,12.7,13.1,1: : Example: 10 rock density measurements 12.5,13.2,11.8,12.7,13.1,12.9,12.3,13.0,12.6,12.8 (g/cm³, 95% confidence, sample) → mean=12.6900, standard deviation=0.4175, CV=3.29%, median=12.7500, range=1.4000, SE=0.1320, t(0.025,9)=2.262, margin of error=0.2987, 95% CI [12.3913, 12.9887], judged "uniform". Switching to ore grades 1.2,1.8,0.9,2.3,1.5,1.1,0.7,2.0,1.6,3.1 → mean=1.6200, σ=0.7193, CV=44.40%, judged "non-uniform".
map.95% 置信区间怎么理解？: How should a 95% confidence interval be read?
map.在重复抽样下，约 95% 的此类区间会覆盖真实总体均值；它描述的是估计的不确定性: Under repeated sampling, about 95% of such intervals cover the true population mean; it describes the uncertainty of the estimate, not a "95% probability that the truth lies in this interval". The larger the sample and the smaller the dispersion, the narrower the interval.
map.若这 n 个数据就是研究对象的全部（如整批样品），用总体(N)方差；若只是从更大: If these n values are the entire population under study (e.g. a whole batch of samples), use the population (N) variance; if they are only a sample from a larger population, use the sample (n−1) variance for an unbiased estimate — inferential statistics must use the sample.
